HAI 21.03 — HIL-based Augmented ICS Security Dataset [test] — prepared from hai-21.03-test1.csv.gz, downsampled to every 10th row, dropped attack_P1, attack_P2, attack_P3 | test slice of a three-way split, train_fraction=0.04 calib_fraction=0.3 | Coarse-map inflation: HAI's declared topology could not be partitioned below process level for P1 and P2, so unrelated departures anywhere on one process collapse into a single subsystem event. A large reduction here is evidence that grouping is correctly IMPLEMENTED, not that it is correctly RESOLVED. A finer map would lower the headline number and raise its meaning. | Uncalibrated hypothesis confidence: the confidences on these hypotheses are NOT calibrated probabilities and must not be surfaced to a user under Constitution §3.3. Three reasons, and the third is measured rather than asserted. (1) The template priors are reasoned placeholders, not measured base rates. (2) EVIDENCE_STRENGTH is a placeholder too, and measuring either needs data labelling WHICH EXPLANATION IS TRUE, which no corpus PHOS uses carries — HAI labels attack and normal. (3) The belief update treats each subsystem event as independent, and on a plant they are plainly not: one disturbance persisting across consecutive windows arrives as many near-identical events, so a confidence built from them counts one cause many times. Atlas may rank and reason over these hypotheses; it may not present their confidences as calibrated. Evidence weights, separately, are calibrated. | Co-occurring-fault masking: a coarse group can hide a second, unrelated event inside one subsystem event. Two independent faults on one process are indistinguishable from one, and an attack co-occurring with a fault is reported as a single thing to investigate. That is a recall risk carried by the grouping, not a win. | Grouped weight is a maximum: a subsystem event carries the strongest member's calibrated weight, and a maximum over a set of calibrated probabilities is not itself a calibrated probability — it is biased upward by how many signals the unit carries. The calibration error reported for subsystem events may therefore come out better or worse than the per-signal one for reasons that have nothing to do with the calibrator, and is not a reading of it.

CERT Insider Threat r3.1 (CMU/SEI, doi:10.1184/R1/12841247.v1) | 2721368 observations over 1000 users x 8 features, one-day windows | 2 labelled insider(s): CSF0929/scenario-1, CCH0959/scenario-2 | base rate 53 malicious of 340171 user-windows | CERT is SYNTHETIC: simulated users and simulated attackers, not observed enterprise activity. A good number here demonstrates the machinery works; it does not demonstrate real-world capability, and simulated insiders may be cleaner and more obvious than real ones. | The featurisation is a per-entity STARTER set (8 count features over a one-day window). There is no relationship context (PART 6A) and no peer-group baselining (PART 6B), so this baseline is expected to miss the insider whose own history looks unremarkable and whose peers' does not — which is the class 6B exists to catch. | Ground truth is ENTITY-SCOPED: a detection counts only when it names the labelled malicious user inside their labelled window. The false-positive denominator is normal USER-hours summed across the population, not wall-clock hours, and is not comparable to an Atlas FP rate. | test half of a train_fraction=0.5 attack-free-prefix split

CERT Insider Threat r3.1 (CMU/SEI, doi:10.1184/R1/12841247.v1) | 1000 directory users | 5481164 test observations x 26 features (sentiel-enriched-v1), one-day windows | 2 labelled insider(s) in the test half: CSF0929/scenario-1, CCH0959/scenario-2 | test half of a train_fraction=0.5 attack-free-prefix split | base rate 53 malicious of 210814 user-windows | CERT is SYNTHETIC: simulated users and simulated attackers, not observed enterprise activity. A good number here demonstrates the machinery works; it does not demonstrate real-world capability, and simulated insiders may be cleaner and more obvious than real ones. | Ground truth is ENTITY-SCOPED: a detection counts only when it names the labelled malicious user inside their labelled window. The false-positive denominator is normal USER-hours summed across the population, not wall-clock hours, and is not comparable to an Atlas FP rate. | The featurisation is the PART 6A ENRICHED per-entity set: 26 features over a one-day window — the 8 starter counts, a signed z-score of each against that user's own trailing history, a first difference and a trailing slope for the 3 signals CERT's own scenario descriptions frame as an onset or escalation, and 4 first-order relationship summaries. This SUPERSEDES the starter-set caveat carried by phos.sentiel.SENTIEL_CAVEATS. | Still NO PEER CONTEXT. Every feature is computed from one user's own events and one user's own history. The insider who is unremarkable against their own past and remarkable against their team's is still invisible, and that is the class PART 6B exists to catch. Richer per-entity features are not a substitute for it and this run does not test it. | BASELINE-RELATIVE FEATURES OVERFIT A SHORT HISTORY. A user barely past the cold-start boundary has a trailing mean and spread estimated from a handful of windows, so their deviations swing on little evidence. The cold-start policy makes the boundary explicit — every baseline-relative read is a documented neutral 0.0 until the history is long enough — but the windows just past it are noisy and are counted like any other. | ONLY 2 USERS are labelled malicious in r3.1, so window recall can take only the values 0, 0.5 and 1.0. It is not independently quotable and must not be read as a continuous rate. Precision, and its multiple over the trivial alert-on-everything floor, are the honest headline. | SIDE-BY-SIDE vs PART 6·D (commit ba41b99, cert-r3.1-user-day-test, 8 features): precision 0.004061 = 16.15x the alert-on-everything floor. THIS RUN (26 features): precision 0.003147 = 12.52x that floor (53 malicious of 210814 test user-windows). VERDICT: WORSE (0.77x the reference multiple). Window recall 1.0 is not quotable at 2 insiders.

CERT r3.1 episode queue over 210,814 scored entity-days (34 features), 40 episodes | An EPISODE IS A LARGER UNIT OF READING THAN AN ENTITY-DAY. Compressing N entity-days into M episodes is a gain only if an analyst can work an episode for less than the N/M days it replaces. Every episode reports n_days so the trade is visible; no number in this module assumes an episode and a day cost the same to triage. | Two labelled insiders means insider coverage takes only the values 0, 0.5 and 1.0. It is not a rate and must not be read as one. The malicious ENTITY-DAY count (53) is the finer denominator and is the one to read. | This re-counts PART 6B's own scores in a different unit. No model was refitted, no threshold was searched against a label, and the frozen 48-alert row is reproduced as a gate before any number here is computed. It does not supersede that row. | CERT is SYNTHETIC. Simulated insiders may be more persistent, and therefore more episodic, than real ones; a compression ratio measured here is not a claim about an enterprise.

HAI 21.03 — HIL-based Augmented ICS Security Dataset [test] — prepared from hai-21.03-test1.csv.gz, downsampled to every 10th row, dropped attack_P1, attack_P2, attack_P3 | test slice of a three-way split, train_fraction=0.04 calib_fraction=0.3 | Coarse-map inflation: HAI's declared topology could not be partitioned below process level for P1 and P2, so unrelated departures anywhere on one process collapse into a single subsystem event. A large reduction here is evidence that grouping is correctly IMPLEMENTED, not that it is correctly RESOLVED. A finer map would lower the headline number and raise its meaning. | Uncalibrated hypothesis confidence: the confidences on these hypotheses are NOT calibrated probabilities and must not be surfaced to a user under Constitution §3.3. Three reasons, and the third is measured rather than asserted. (1) The template priors are reasoned placeholders, not measured base rates. (2) EVIDENCE_STRENGTH is a placeholder too, and measuring either needs data labelling WHICH EXPLANATION IS TRUE, which no corpus PHOS uses carries — HAI labels attack and normal. (3) The belief update treats each subsystem event as independent, and on a plant they are plainly not: one disturbance persisting across consecutive windows arrives as many near-identical events, so a confidence built from them counts one cause many times. Atlas may rank and reason over these hypotheses; it may not present their confidences as calibrated. Evidence weights, separately, are calibrated. | Co-occurring-fault masking: a coarse group can hide a second, unrelated event inside one subsystem event. Two independent faults on one process are indistinguishable from one, and an attack co-occurring with a fault is reported as a single thing to investigate. That is a recall risk carried by the grouping, not a win. | Grouped weight is a maximum: a subsystem event carries the strongest member's calibrated weight, and a maximum over a set of calibrated probabilities is not itself a calibrated probability — it is biased upward by how many signals the unit carries. The calibration error reported for subsystem events may therefore come out better or worse than the per-signal one for reasons that have nothing to do with the calibrator, and is not a reading of it. | Saturated false-positive load: when a declared SaturationPolicy fires, the row is REFUSED as a detection claim even if recall looks excellent. Metrics stay on the report; they must not be quoted as detection. Public distillation 18.72 and Data4Cyber Track A keep their log names and stay MEASURED unless a caller applies a policy. Do not raise dwell_samples to chase a quieter public ZIP. | Normal-score CDF weights are not attack probabilities: the map is the empirical CDF of held-out attack-free magnitudes (ADR 0083). A weight of 0.9 means the score sits at or above about 90% of ordinary scores the model saw on normal data — not that an attack is 90% likely. Do not quote ECE against attack labels as evidence that these weights are calibrated probabilities under Constitution §3.3.
